fields.description: The region the metric is published in. The account's region is listed first.

fields.description: AWS service namespaces (AWS/Lambda) or your own custom namespace. CloudWatch only lists metrics that reported data in the past two weeks; type a namespace to use one that is not listed.

options.label: Sum

fields.label: Query

credentialFields.label: Cluster hourly rates
credentialFields.description: Optional. Hourly prices used to derive workload costs. Clusters opened from their cloud account get node prices automatically. Otherwise list instance types: s-2vcpu-4gb=0.0357, m5.large=0.096. Other keys: controlPlane=0.10 (flat fee), loadBalancer=0.0149 (per LoadBalancer Service), storage/*=0.10 or storage/gp3=0.08 (per GiB-month), network/cross_zone=0.01 and network/internet_egress=0.09 (per GB), gpu/a100-80gb=3.93 or gpu/*=2.50 (per GPU hour). Left blank, capacity and efficiency are still shown without cost.

credentialFields.label: GPU metrics source
credentialFields.description: Optional. Where GPU utilization comes from, for idle-GPU cost and GPU right-sizing. Left blank, the cluster's Prometheus is found automatically (or the NVIDIA DCGM exporter pods are sampled directly). Set it to namespace/service:port to name a Prometheus that scrapes the DCGM or AMD exporter, or to none to turn GPU metrics off.

credentialFields.label: Node labels for cost
credentialFields.description: Optional. Which node labels become cost dimensions, so spend can be grouped and filtered by them (for example by team, or by a label your autoscaler sets). Instance type, zone, node pool and spot or on-demand capacity are always recorded. Left blank, the standard topology labels plus team, owner, environment and cost-center are used where your nodes have them. Pick up to 20; choose none to record no extra labels.

credentialFields.label: Volume labels for cost
credentialFields.description: Optional. Which PersistentVolumeClaim labels become cost dimensions on volume cost. Storage class is always recorded. Left blank, the standard app.kubernetes.io labels plus team, owner, environment and cost-center are used where your claims have them. Pick up to 20; choose none to record no extra labels.

fields.description: Return a "day" column (date) and a "value" column (number), plus an optional "label" column for a breakdown. {{from}} and {{to}} are the first and last day of the window (inclusive), {{to_exclusive}} is the day after {{to}}, and {{timezone}} is the importer's timezone. Days are taken as written, so convert timestamps yourself, for example DATE(CONVERT_TZ(created_at, 'UTC', {{timezone}})), which needs the server's time zone tables loaded.
fields.placeholder:
SELECT DATE(created_at) AS day, COUNT(*) AS value
FROM signups
WHERE created_at >= {{from}} AND created_at < {{to_exclusive}}
GROUP BY 1

resourceTypes.description: The Sentry organization this connection reads. Shows month-to-date usage per data category (accepted, filtered and rate limited), an estimated cost, and daily usage charts.
A Sentry project. Shows its platform, teams, events accepted and dropped in the last 24 hours, and unresolved issues. Create, rename, change platform or delete.
A Sentry team: who owns which projects. Shows its members and projects. Create, rename or delete a team.
A release of your code, as reported to Sentry. Shows when it was created and released, its projects, new issues it introduced, commits and its last deploy. The 100 most recent releases are listed.
An unresolved Sentry issue. The 100 issues with the most events in the last 14 days are listed. Resolve it, archive it until it escalates or for good, or reopen it, and chart its events.
A project's client key: the DSN your SDKs send events with. Shows whether it is enabled and its rate limit. Create one, rename it, change its rate limit, enable or disable it, or delete it.

manifest.description: Data cloud. Track Snowflake spend by service and warehouse (billed when the role can read organization usage, estimated from credits otherwise), the remaining capacity balance, and query cost by tag, user and role; manage warehouses, databases, schemas, resource monitors, users, roles, tasks, pipes and dynamic tables, and run SQL.
manifest.author: Infrawrench

credentialFields.label: Account
credentialFields.description: Your account identifier (orgname-accountname) or any Snowflake URL for the account: the Snowsight address (app.snowflake.com/<org>/<account>) or the account URL (<org>-<account>.snowflakecomputing.com). Find it under your name, Account, View account details.

credentialFields.label: User
credentialFields.description: The Snowflake user to connect as. A dedicated service user (TYPE = SERVICE) is best.

credentialFields.label: Private Key or Access Token
credentialFields.description: Either the user's unencrypted RSA private key in PEM form (key-pair authentication: register the public key with ALTER USER ... SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY), or a programmatic access token. Access tokens need the user to be covered by a network policy unless an authentication policy relaxes that.

credentialFields.label: Role
credentialFields.description: The role queries run as. Cost and usage need the SNOWFLAKE database role USAGE_VIEWER (or IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on SNOWFLAKE); billed cost and the capacity balance need the organization usage views (ORGADMIN or GLOBALORGADMIN).

credentialFields.label: Warehouse
credentialFields.description: Where usage and cost queries run. An X-Small warehouse with a 60 second auto-suspend is plenty; listing resources never resumes it.

credentialFields.label: Price per Credit
credentialFields.description: Used only when the role cannot read organization usage. List price on AWS US East is 2.00 (Standard), 3.00 (Enterprise) or 4.00 (Business Critical) USD; enter your contract rate.

credentialFields.label: Storage Price per TB-Month
credentialFields.description: Used only for estimated cost. 23.00 USD on a capacity contract in AWS US East; on-demand is higher.

credentialFields.label: Data Transfer Price per TB
credentialFields.description: Used only for estimated cost. Snowflake prices egress per cloud and region pair, so transfer is left out of estimates until you enter a rate.

credentialFields.label: Price Currency
credentialFields.description: Currency of the prices above (ISO code). Billed cost uses your contract currency regardless.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

businessMetricSource.label: Snowflake SQL
businessMetricSource.description: Run a Snowflake SQL query on a schedule. It must return one row per day with a `day` and a `value` column, plus an optional `label` column for a breakdown.

fields.label: Warehouse
fields.description: The warehouse the query runs on, and which is billed for it. Leave empty to use the account's warehouse.

fields.label: Role
fields.description: Optional. The role the query runs as. Snowflake cannot make a session read-only, so pick a role that can only read the data the query needs. Leave empty to use the account's role.

fields.label: Database
fields.description: Default database: unqualified table names resolve here.

fields.label: Schema
fields.description: Optional default schema within the database.

fields.label: Query
fields.description: A single SELECT returning `day`, `value` and optionally `label`. {{from}}, {{to}}, {{to_exclusive}} and {{timezone}} are replaced with quoted values for the import window. The session timezone is the importer's timezone, so casting a TIMESTAMP_LTZ to DATE gives local days.
fields.placeholder:
SELECT created_at::date AS day, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS value
FROM orders
WHERE created_at::date BETWEEN {{from}} AND {{to}}
GROUP BY day

warehouseSink.label: Snowflake table
warehouseSink.description: Load rows into a table in your Snowflake account through the SQL API. The table is created on the first run if it does not exist.

targetFields.label: Warehouse
targetFields.description: Runs the load. An X-Small warehouse with auto-suspend is plenty.

targetFields.label: Table
targetFields.description: Pick an existing table or type a new name; a new table is created.

resourceTypes.description: The connected Snowflake account. Shows spend by service, the remaining capacity balance when the role can see organization usage, credits by warehouse, cost attributed to query tags, users, roles and warehouses, and warehouse recommendations.
A virtual warehouse: the compute Snowflake bills credits for while it runs. Suspend, resume, resize, change auto-suspend, assign a resource monitor, chart credits and query load, and run SQL on it.

orphanRule.reason: Running with auto-suspend turned off, so it bills credits for every idle second until someone suspends it.

fields.label: Size
fields.description: Each size up doubles the credits per hour (X-Small is 1 credit an hour) and roughly the compute.

fields.label: Auto-Suspend (seconds)
fields.description: Seconds of inactivity before the warehouse suspends. 0 means it never suspends. Snowflake bills at least 60 seconds every time a warehouse resumes, so 60 to 300 seconds suits most workloads.

fields.label: Auto-Resume
fields.description: Resume automatically when a query arrives.

fields.label: Max Clusters
fields.description: Above 1 makes this a multi-cluster warehouse (Enterprise edition and up).

fields.label: Scaling Policy
fields.description: STANDARD starts clusters as soon as queries queue; ECONOMY waits until a new cluster would be kept busy for six minutes.

fields.label: Time Travel Retention (days)

resourceTypes.description: A schema in a Snowflake database. Change its retention or comment, or run SQL in it.

fields.label: Notify At (%)
fields.description: Comma-separated percentages of the quota that send an email, e.g. 75,90.

fields.label: Suspend At (%)
fields.description: Suspend the warehouses once running queries finish.

fields.label: Suspend Immediately At (%)

resourceTypes.description: The Anyscale organization the API key belongs to. Shows Anyscale spend this month by workload type, project and user, and the remaining balance of every credit grant and prepaid commit, and charts daily spend.

An Anyscale cloud: where clusters run. Either customer-hosted (your AWS account, Google Cloud project or Kubernetes cluster, whose machines are billed by that provider) or Anyscale-hosted. Charts node count by market type, CPU and GPU count and utilization, and spot preemptions across every cluster in the cloud.
An Anyscale project: groups workspaces, jobs and services inside a cloud. Create and delete projects, and chart the node count and utilization of the clusters running in one.
An Anyscale workspace: an interactive development cluster. Start and terminate it, see whether Anyscale considers it idle and when auto-termination will stop it, and see what it has cost.

orphanRule.reason: Workspace is running but idle: no Ray, command or editor activity

fields.label: Idle
fields.description: Running with no Ray, command or editor activity, as Anyscale reports it.

resourceTypes.description: An Anyscale job: a batch workload on its own cluster. Shows state, the last run, retries, its schedule or queue, and what it has cost; terminate a running job.

An Anyscale service: a Ray Serve deployment. Shows its state, rollout progress between the primary and canary versions and their traffic weights, endpoint and cost; roll back a rollout or terminate the service.
An Anyscale compute config: the head and worker node types, autoscaling bounds, spot usage and auto-termination a cluster launches with. Archive configs nobody uses.

An Anyscale budget: a daily or monthly soft limit on Anyscale spend for the organization, a cloud, or a project in a cloud, which alerts when crossed. Create, edit, enable, disable and delete budgets.

fields.label: Amount
fields.description: The limit, in the unit below.

fields.label: Unit
fields.description: US dollars, or Anyscale credits.

fields.label: Period
fields.description: Daily budgets reset at midnight UTC; monthly budgets on the 1st.

manifest.description: Observability platform for logs, metrics and traces. Track usage and estimated cost by pillar and TCO priority, watch the daily quota, and manage alerts, dashboards, TCO policies, parsing rules, enrichments, webhooks and Events2Metrics.
manifest.author: Infrawrench

credentialFields.label: Coralogix Region
credentialFields.description: The region (Coralogix domain) your team lives in, read from the address you sign in at: team.coralogix.com is EU1, team.app.eu2.coralogix.com is EU2, team.app.coralogix.us is US1, team.app.cx498.coralogix.com is US2. Keys only work in their own region.

credentialFields.label: API Key
credentialFields.description: A Team API key from Settings, API Keys (a Personal key works too, with its owner's permissions). Attach the DataUsage preset for usage and cost, and the Alerts, Dashboards, TCOPolicies, ParsingRules, Enrichments, OutboundWebhooks and Events2Metrics presets for the matching resources. Not a Send-Your-Data key: those only ingest data.

credentialFields.label: Price per Unit (USD)
credentialFields.description: What one Coralogix unit costs on your plan. Coralogix reports usage in units, not money, so cost is units multiplied by this price. Leave the published $1.50 per unit or enter your contracted rate. You can edit it later.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

capabilities.label: Data usage and cost
capabilities.description: Daily units and GB by pillar and TCO priority, priced into estimated cost, and the team's daily quota usage.

requiredPermissions.label: Enable and disable Data Usage Metrics

capabilities.label: Alerts
capabilities.description: List alert definitions and their trigger history; edit, enable and disable them.

capabilities.label: TCO policies
capabilities.description: List TCO policies, change their priority and chart the volume they match.

capabilities.label: Quota rules
capabilities.description: How the daily quota is shared between entity types, and editing it.

resourceTypes.description: The Coralogix team the API key belongs to. Shows this month's units, GB and estimated cost by pillar and TCO priority, today's use of the daily unit quota, and configuration limits.
A Coralogix alert definition. Edit its name, description and priority, enable or disable it, and chart how often it has triggered.

fields.label: Priority
fields.description: P1 is the most severe, P5 the least.

resourceTypes.description: A Coralogix custom dashboard. Pin or unpin it, make it the team's default dashboard, or delete it.

A TCO Optimizer policy: routes matching logs, spans or RUM events to a priority (High for Frequent Search, Medium for Monitoring, Low for Compliance, or Block), which sets the units per GB. Edit its priority, name and description, or enable or disable it.

fields.label: Priority
fields.description: High is fully indexed for Frequent Search, Medium keeps data for Monitoring (alerts, dashboards, Events2Metrics), Low sends it straight to the archive for Compliance, Block drops it. Lower priorities cost fewer units per GB.

resourceTypes.description: A group of parsing rules that parse, extract, replace or block log data as it arrives. Enable or disable the group, or delete it.
An enrichment rule that adds Geo IP, suspicious IP, AWS resource or custom lookup data to a log field as it arrives. Create one against a field and a lookup you pick, or delete it.
A custom enrichment lookup table uploaded to Coralogix as a CSV file. Enrichment rules use it to add columns to matching logs.
An outbound webhook alerts notify through: Slack, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Microsoft Teams, Jira, email groups, Amazon EventBridge or a generic HTTP endpoint. Send a test notification, or delete it.

How the team's daily unit quota is shared between entity types (logs, spans, metrics, session recordings...). Change an entity type's allocation, whether it may overflow into unused quota, or switch the rule off.

fields.label: Allocation
fields.description: A percentage of the daily quota, or a fixed number of units when the allocation type is Locked units.

fields.label: Can Overflow
fields.description: Let this entity type use quota other entity types leave unused.

resourceTypes.description: An Events2Metrics rule that turns matching logs or spans into metrics, so the raw events can be routed to a cheaper TCO priority. Shows its query, the metrics and labels it produces and its permutation limit; delete it.

manifest.description: Cursor team administration: members and seats (with idle-seat detection), per-user spend limits, billing and member groups, repository blocklists, usage by model and member, and daily cost from usage-based spend plus seat estimates. Enterprise teams also get the Analytics and AI Code Tracking series.
manifest.author: Infrawrench

credentialFields.label: Admin API Key
credentialFields.description: A team API key created by a team admin in the Cursor dashboard under Settings, API Keys. Starts with crsr_. A read-only key lists everything and collects costs; editing needs the admin scope. Teams and Enterprise plans only.

credentialFields.label: Standard seat price (USD per month)
credentialFields.description: What one standard Cursor seat costs you per month. Cursor's API does not report seat pricing, so seat costs are estimated from this. Defaults to the published Teams price of $40; set your negotiated or annual rate here.

credentialFields.label: Premium seat price (USD per month)
credentialFields.description: What one premium seat costs you per month. Defaults to the published price of $120.

credentialFields.label: Premium seat members
credentialFields.description: Emails of the members on premium seats, separated by commas. Everyone else with a paid seat is priced as standard; unpaid admins are never charged.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

capabilities.label: Members, spend and usage
capabilities.description: List members, read spend this cycle, daily usage and usage events, and collect costs.

requiredPermissions.label: Team API key (read-only or admin scope)

capabilities.label: Spend limits, groups and blocklists
capabilities.description: Set per-user spend limits, manage billing and member groups and repository blocklists, remove members.

requiredPermissions.label: Team API key with the admin scope

capabilities.label: Analytics and AI Code Tracking
capabilities.description: Daily active users by surface, agent edit and Tab acceptance, client versions and AI-attributed commit lines.

requiredPermissions.label: Team API key with the admin scope

resourceTypes.description: Your Cursor team: seats, spend this billing cycle, and team-wide usage metrics (active users, requests by feature, included vs usage-based requests, accepted lines and Tab acceptance). Enterprise teams also get the Analytics API series and AI-attributed commit lines. The Logs tab shows the team audit log.

A member of the Cursor team with their role, seat, last activity, spend this billing cycle and per-user spend limit. Edit to set or clear the spend limit (whole US dollars). Delete removes the member from the team; Cursor keeps the seat billed until the end of the cycle. Members with no activity in 30 days are flagged as idle seats.

orphanRule.reason: Paid Cursor seat with no editor, agent or Bugbot activity in the last 30 days

fields.label: Spend limit (USD)
fields.description: Hard limit on this member's usage-based spend per billing cycle, in whole US dollars. Leave empty to remove the member's own limit (the team or group limit then applies).

resourceTypes.description: A model your team used in the last 30 days, from Cursor's usage events: requests (included vs usage-based), Max Mode share, tokens, usage-based spend and how many members used it. Read-only.
A Cursor billing group, used to attribute spend to a department or cost centre. Shows spend this billing cycle, daily spend and members. Create, rename, change members (by email) or delete.

fields.label: Member emails
fields.description: Comma-separated emails of the team members in this group. Add or remove addresses to change membership; every address must belong to a team member.

resourceTypes.description: A Cursor team directory group with its monthly spending limit and members. Create, rename, set or clear the spending limit, change members (by email) or delete.

fields.label: Member emails
fields.description: Comma-separated emails of the team members in this group. Add or remove addresses to change membership; every address must belong to a team member.

fields.label: Monthly spending limit (USD)
fields.description: Whole US dollars per member per month, 0 to 2,147,483,647. Leave empty to remove the limit.

resourceTypes.description: Glob patterns of files Cursor will not index or send to models for a repository (for example .env files or a secrets directory). Create, edit the patterns, or delete.

fields.label: Blocked patterns
fields.description: Comma-separated glob patterns, for example *.env, config/*, secrets/**

manifest.description: Monitoring and observability. Track Datadog spend by product and organization with month-end projections, chart hourly usage, and manage monitors, downtimes, dashboards, SLOs, synthetic tests, hosts, users and keys.
manifest.author: Infrawrench

credentialFields.label: Datadog Site
credentialFields.description: The Datadog site your organization lives on: the one in the address you sign in at (app.datadoghq.com is US1, app.datadoghq.eu is EU, us5.datadoghq.com is US5). Keys only work against their own site.

credentialFields.label: API Key
credentialFields.description: A Datadog API key from Organization Settings, API Keys. It identifies the organization. For cost data, use a key from the parent organization: child organizations cannot read cost.

credentialFields.label: Application Key
credentialFields.description: A Datadog application key from Organization Settings, Application Keys (or Personal Settings for your own). It carries its owner's permissions. Cost data needs Usage Read and Billing Read. For a read-only account, use a scoped key with only the read scopes listed under Check credentials.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

capabilities.label: Cost data
capabilities.description: Estimated, projected and historical cost by product and organization, and cost attribution by tag. Both keys must belong to the parent organization.

capabilities.label: Usage metrics
capabilities.description: Hourly usage by product on each organization's Metrics tab.

capabilities.label: Monitors and downtimes
capabilities.description: List monitors and downtimes, edit monitors, mute and schedule downtimes.

capabilities.label: Synthetic tests
capabilities.description: List tests and chart results; pause, resume and run them.

capabilities.label: Host and monitor charts
capabilities.description: Metric queries behind the host and monitor Metrics tabs.

capabilities.label: Business metric import
capabilities.description: Reading a metric on a schedule as a unit-cost denominator: listing metrics and their tags, then querying the series.

capabilities.label: Users
capabilities.description: List users and disable them from the access review.

businessMetricSource.label: Datadog metric
businessMetricSource.description: Read a Datadog metric, such as requests served, orders placed or a custom metric your application sends, and store one value per day.

fields.label: Metric
fields.description: Metrics that reported in the past week are listed. Type a name to use one that is not.

fields.label: Scope
fields.description: Which sources to include, as Datadog tags: env:prod, or several separated by commas to require all of them. * reads every source.

fields.label: Break down by
fields.description: Optional tag key. Each value becomes its own label on the metric, and a day's total is the sum across them.

fields.label: Combine sources with
fields.description: How values reported by several hosts or containers at once are combined.

fields.label: Count metric
fields.description: For count and rate metrics, read the number of events rather than the per-second rate Datadog stores.

options.label: Yes, read it as a count

fields.label: Hourly rollup
fields.description: How each hour is summarized before the importer combines hours into days. Sum suits counts; for averages a daily figure combines hourly values, so it is an approximation.

resourceTypes.description: A Datadog organization (the parent, or each child on a multi-organization account). Shows month-to-date and projected cost by product, cost attribution by tag, and hourly usage.
A Datadog monitor. Edit its name, notification message, priority and tags, mute it for a while or until you unmute it, and chart the metric a metric or query alert watches.

fields.label: Notification Message
fields.description: Sent with every notification. Mention recipients with @-handles, exactly as in Datadog.

fields.label: Priority
fields.description: 1 is the most severe, 5 the least. Leave blank for no priority.

fields.label: Tags
fields.description: Comma-separated, for example team:payments, env:prod.

resourceTypes.description: A scheduled Datadog downtime that silences monitors for a scope and a time window. Create one for a monitor you pick or for every monitor in a scope, change its message or scope, or cancel it.

fields.label: Scope
fields.description: Which groups are silenced: * for everything, or tags like env:prod.

resourceTypes.description: A Datadog dashboard. Open it in Datadog or delete it.
A Datadog service level objective. Charts the SLI and the remaining error budget over the selected window.
A Datadog Synthetic Monitoring test: API, browser, mobile or network. Pause or resume it, run it now from every configured location, and chart response time and failures from recent results.
A host reporting to Datadog, usually through the Datadog Agent. Shows the Agent version, platform and integrations, mutes or unmutes it, and charts CPU, load, memory and network.
A member of the Datadog organization, including service accounts. Shows roles, MFA and last login, and disables a user.

A Datadog API key: the organization-level credential Agents and integrations send data with. Listed by name, last four characters, creator and last use; the key itself is never shown again after creation.
A Datadog application key: a user's or service account's credential for the API, optionally narrowed to scopes. Listed with owner, scopes and last use.

credentialFields.description: The ID half of a Modal API token, from Settings, API Tokens in the Modal dashboard (or `token_id` in ~/.modal.toml after `modal token new`). A token sees every environment of its workspace. Cost data needs a Team or Enterprise workspace.

credentialFields.label: Token Secret
credentialFields.description: The secret half of the same token. Modal shows it only once, when the token is created.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

resourceTypes.description: The Modal workspace the token belongs to. Shows this month's metered and billed cost with the credits and other adjustments between them, cost by product, the workspace rate card, and charts cost per day by resource type and GPU hours.

A Modal environment: an isolated set of apps, secrets, volumes, dicts and queues. Create, rename or delete one, set its concurrency limits and web endpoint suffix, and see its spend this cycle against its budget and its cost per day.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: Letters, numbers, dashes and underscores. Apps address the environment by it.

fields.label: Web Endpoint Suffix
fields.description: Added to the URLs of this environment's web endpoints so they do not collide with another environment's.

fields.label: Max Concurrent Containers
fields.description: Cap on containers running at once in this environment. Leave empty for no cap.

fields.label: Max Concurrent GPUs
fields.description: Cap on GPUs in use at once in this environment. Leave empty for no cap.

resourceTypes.description: A Modal app: deployed, ephemeral or stopped. Shows its functions and servers with their GPUs and schedules, its tags and deployment history, and charts its cost per day by resource type. Stop a running app from its detail page.

A function, class or server of a deployed Modal app. Shows its GPU, CPU and memory, autoscaling (min, max and buffer containers, scale-down window), input concurrency, timeouts and schedule, its live backlog and running inputs, and charts inputs by outcome, cold starts, latency and container utilization.
A function of a deployed Modal app that runs on a cron or fixed-period schedule, with its schedule, GPU and app, and the same invocation charts as any function.
A Modal volume: a persistent, distributed file system apps mount. Shows its version and who created it. Deleting a volume deletes every file in it.
A Modal secret: a named set of environment variables functions read at run time. Lists its key names and when it was last used; values are never read.
A named Modal dict: a distributed key-value store shared between functions.
A named Modal queue: a distributed FIFO shared between functions, with its partition count and the number of items waiting.

resourceTypes.description: The Temporal Cloud account the API key belongs to: its id, the identity and role of the key, the metrics endpoint, and the regions namespaces can be placed in.

A Temporal Cloud namespace: the unit of isolation for workflows, with its own region, retention, authentication and endpoints. Edit retention, delete protection, API key authentication, the codec server and tags; manage search attributes; add a replica region and fail over.

fields.label: Description
fields.description: Up to 255 printable ASCII characters.

fields.label: Retention (days)
fields.description: How long closed workflow histories are kept, from 1 to 90 days. A change applies to workflows that close after it; longer retention raises retained storage cost.

fields.label: Delete Protection
fields.description: When on, the namespace cannot be deleted until protection is turned off.

fields.label: API Key Authentication
fields.description: Allow clients to connect with API keys. Turning it off disconnects every client that uses one.

fields.label: Codec Server Endpoint
fields.description: HTTPS URL of the codec server the Temporal Cloud UI uses to decode payloads. Leave empty for none.

fields.label: Tags
fields.description: Comma-separated key=value pairs, up to 10, for example team=payments, env=prod. Keys and values use lowercase letters, digits, and . _ - @. Tags flow into the billing report, so they break cost down too.

resourceTypes.description: A workflow history export sink: closed workflow histories from the namespace are written to your S3 or GCS bucket. Shows health and the last export, enables or disables it, edits the destination and validates access.
A person in the Temporal Cloud account with an account role and per-namespace permissions. Invite users, change their account role, grant or change namespace access, and remove them.

fields.label: Account Role
fields.description: admin manages everything except owners; developer creates namespaces and Nexus endpoints; financeadmin reads and manages billing; read is read-only; metricsread can only read metrics. Owners are managed in Temporal Cloud.

resourceTypes.description: A machine identity in the Temporal Cloud account. Account-scoped ones carry an account role plus namespace permissions; namespace-scoped ones are bound to one namespace.

fields.label: Account Role
fields.description: Ignored for namespace-scoped service accounts.

resourceTypes.description: A Temporal Cloud API key owned by a user or a service account. Listed with owner, expiry and state; disable or enable it, change its name or description, or delete it. The secret itself is never shown again after creation.
A Nexus endpoint: a stable name other namespaces call to reach operations served by workers on a target namespace and task queue. Create, retarget, change which namespaces may call it, and delete.

fields.label: Name

fields.label: Target Namespace

resourceTypes.description: A connectivity rule for how namespaces are reached: public internet (optionally with stable IPs) or a private connection such as AWS PrivateLink or GCP Private Service Connect. Attach it to namespaces from the namespace page.

manifest.description: Observability for distributed systems. credentialFields.description: Optional, but needed to list every environment and manage API keys. You can paste the joined id:secret value here.

Give it Manage Queries and Columns, Run Queries, Manage Triggers, Manage SLOs, Manage Public Boards, Manage Markers and Manage Recipients. Other environments can be connected later from their own page.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)

capabilities.label: Datasets and columns

resourceTypes.description: A Honeycomb dataset: where one service's (or one source's) events land. Edit its description, JSON unpacking depth, delete protection and the columns Honeycomb treats as trace id, duration, error and so on, and chart event volume, latency percentiles and error rate.

fields.label: JSON Unpacking Depth
fields.description: How many levels of nested JSON fields Honeycomb unpacks into columns (0 to 10).

fields.label: Delete Protection
fields.description: While on, the dataset cannot be deleted. Turn it off before deleting.

fields.label: Trace ID Column
fields.description: Column holding the trace id. Leave blank for Honeycomb's default.

fields.label: Duration Column
fields.description: Column holding the span duration in milliseconds. Feeds the latency charts.

fields.label: Error Column
fields.description: Column that is set when a span failed. Feeds the error rate chart.

resourceTypes.description: A column in a dataset. Change its type, description or visibility, add one before events carry it, or delete one nobody sends any more.

fields.label: Type
fields.description: histogram applies to metrics datasets only.

fields.label: Hidden
fields.description: Hidden columns are left out of autocomplete and raw data views.

fields.label: Dataset
fields.description: Empty for environment-wide objects.

resourceTypes.description: A calculated field: a formula Honeycomb evaluates on every event at query time. SLOs use one as their SLI. Edit its formula and description, or create one for a dataset or for the whole environment.

fields.label: Expression
fields.description: Derived column formula, for example IF(EXISTS($error), 0, 1).

fields.label: Dataset
fields.description: Empty for environment-wide objects.

resourceTypes.description: A Honeycomb trigger: a query run on a schedule that notifies recipients when its result crosses a threshold. Enable or disable it, change its threshold, frequency and alert behaviour, and chart the query against the threshold.

fields.label: Times Exceeded Before Alerting
fields.description: How many consecutive evaluations must cross the threshold (1 to 5).

fields.label: Frequency (seconds)
fields.description: How often the query runs, in seconds: a multiple of 60 between 60 and 86400, and no shorter than the query's time range allows.

fields.label: Alert When
fields.description: on_change notifies when the trigger fires and resolves, on_true on every evaluation that crosses the threshold, on_group_change per breakdown group.

fields.label: Dataset
fields.description: Empty for environment-wide objects.

fields.label: Target (%)
fields.description: The share of qualifying events expected to succeed, for example 99.9.

fields.label: Window (days)
fields.description: The rolling window the SLO is evaluated over, in days (1 to 90).

fields.label: Dataset
fields.description: Empty for environment-wide objects.

resourceTypes.description: An alert on an SLO's error budget: either when the budget will run out within a time, or when it burns faster than a rate. Edit its thresholds and description, or create one from its SLO.

fields.label: Exhaustion Time (minutes)

fields.label: Budget Rate Window (minutes)
fields.description: Budget-rate alerts: the window the burn rate is measured over.

fields.label: Budget Decrease (%)
fields.description: Budget-rate alerts: notify when the budget drops by this much within the window.

fields.label: Dataset
fields.description: Empty for environment-wide objects.

fields.label: Dataset
fields.description: Empty for environment-wide objects.

fields.label: Dataset

resourceTypes.description: Anomaly detection on one service's error rate or presence, run by Honeycomb. Turn it on or off and change its sensitivity.

fields.label: Dataset
fields.description: Empty for environment-wide objects.

resourceTypes.description: An ingest or configuration key for one environment. Create one with exactly the permissions it needs (its secret is shown once, as the Key output), rename it, disable or enable it, or delete it.

A group of processes Dynatrace treats as one workload (for example all JVMs of one app), with its technologies and the hosts it runs on.

manifest.description: Event, log, trace and metrics storage queried with APL. Manage Axiom datasets, fields, virtual fields, monitors, notifiers, dashboards, views, saved queries, annotations, API tokens and users, query datasets with APL, tail their events, and chart ingest, query compute and plan limits.
manifest.author: Infrawrench

credentialFields.label: API Token
credentialFields.description: An advanced API token from Axiom under Settings, API tokens. Give it read (and, to manage them, create, update and delete) on Datasets, Monitors, Notifiers, Dashboards, Views, Annotations, API tokens and Users, plus Query on the datasets you want to query or chart. A personal access token (Settings, Profile) also works and sees everything you can, but needs the organization below and cannot query edge deployments directly.

credentialFields.label: Organization
credentialFields.description: Only needed with a personal access token: the organization to manage. Picked from the organizations the token can see.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

capabilities.label: Datasets
capabilities.description: List datasets, their fields and virtual fields, and edit them.

capabilities.label: Queries, logs and metrics
capabilities.description: The APL editor, the Logs tab and the Metrics tab run queries. Organization usage charts read the axiom-audit dataset, which needs the Owner role or query access to it.

resourceTypes.description: The Axiom organization the token belongs to: its plan, billing period and the limits its license sets. Charts hourly ingest and query compute from the audit log. Rename it here.

An Axiom dataset of events, logs, traces or metrics. Query it with APL in the query editor, tail its newest events in the Logs tab, chart events and ingested bytes, change its description and retention, trim old data or vacuum unused fields.

fields.label: Custom Retention
fields.description: On to delete events older than the retention below; off keeps them for the plan's default.

resourceTypes.description: A field (column) in a dataset. Set its unit, description and whether it is hidden, or delete it.

fields.label: Unit
fields.description: How Axiom formats values, for example ms, s, bytes or percent.

resourceTypes.description: A field Axiom computes at query time from an APL expression. Create one on a dataset and edit its expression, type, unit and description.

fields.label: Expression
fields.description: An APL expression, for example toint(status) >= 500.

resourceTypes.description: An Axiom monitor: a threshold, match-event or anomaly check on an APL query, run on a schedule. Enable, disable or snooze it, edit its query, threshold and schedule, and chart its query against the threshold with its recent alerts.

fields.label: Operator
fields.description: Threshold monitors: how the query result is compared with the threshold.

resourceTypes.description: Where monitors send alerts: email, Slack, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Microsoft Teams, Discord or a webhook. Create, rename or retarget one, snooze it for a while, or delete it.

fields.label: Target
fields.description: Email: comma-separated addresses. Slack, Teams, Discord webhook, webhook: the URL. Leave PagerDuty and Opsgenie keys blank to keep them.

fields.label: Routing Key or API Key
fields.description: PagerDuty routing key or Opsgenie API key. Leave blank to keep the current one.

resourceTypes.description: An Axiom dashboard of APL and MPL charts. Rename it or change its description, create an empty one, open it in Axiom, or delete it.
A named APL query others can query as if it were a dataset, often used to share part of a dataset. Edit its query and description.
A starred APL query. Its Metrics tab runs the query over the selected time range and charts what it returns.
An annotation: a deploy or other event Axiom marks on the charts of the datasets it names. Add one by hand, or edit its title, description and link.
An Axiom API token with its organization and dataset capabilities. Create one with exactly the capabilities it needs (its value is shown once, as the Token output), regenerate it, or delete it.

outputs.label: Token
outputs.description: Only for tokens created or regenerated from Infrawrench: Axiom shows a token once.

resourceTypes.description: A member of the Axiom organization, with their role. Remove a user from here.

manifest.description: Hosted search. Manage indices and their settings (searchable attributes, ranking, facets, typos, languages, replicas, full settings JSON), copy, move and clear indices, API keys with ACL pickers, A/B tests and crawlers. Synonym and rule counts, API logs, usage, search analytics and cluster latency as metrics, and Algolia's cluster status.
manifest.author: Infrawrench

helpLink.label: Open API Keys in the Algolia dashboard

credentialFields.label: Usage API Key (optional)
credentialFields.description: From Settings, API Keys, under the Usage section. Adds search and write operations, records, data size, processing time, QPS and search capacity charts.

credentialFields.label: Monitoring API Key (optional)
credentialFields.description: From Settings, API Keys, under the Monitoring section (plans with monitoring). Adds the clusters the application runs on, per-cluster search latency and indexing time, and ties status incidents to this application.

credentialFields.label: Analytics Region (optional)
credentialFields.description: Where the application's analytics are stored (United States or Germany), chosen when the application was created. Leave empty to let Algolia route the request.

credentialFields.label: Crawler User ID (optional)
credentialFields.description: In the Crawler admin (crawler.algolia.com) open Settings and copy the Crawler User ID, to manage crawlers.

credentialFields.label: Crawler API Key (optional)
credentialFields.description: The Crawler API Key from the same Crawler settings page.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

manifest.description: Infrastructure monitoring, APM and synthetics from Splunk. Manage detectors, alerts, muting rules, dashboards and charts, teams, members, integrations, access tokens, SLOs and synthetic tests, chart any detector or chart's SignalFlow, and track usage against your organization's limits.

In Splunk Observability Cloud open Settings, Access Tokens, New Token, choose API token and the power role (read_only lists without editing). Managing access tokens, members and integrations needs a token tied to an admin: use an admin's user API access token from your profile instead.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

capabilities.label: Organization and content
capabilities.description: Read the organization, detectors, dashboards, charts, teams, muting rules, alerts and SLOs.

capabilities.label: Detectors and alerts
capabilities.description: List, edit and toggle detectors; clear alerts.

capabilities.label: Access tokens
capabilities.description: List, edit, rotate and delete organization access tokens.

capabilities.label: Members
capabilities.description: Invite and remove users and change admin rights.

capabilities.label: Integrations
capabilities.description: List, toggle, validate and delete integrations.

capabilities.label: Synthetic tests
capabilities.description: List, pause, resume, run and delete synthetic tests.

The Metrics tab charts usage (active metric time series against the limit, data points received, hosts and containers monitored).
A detector: a SignalFlow program whose detect() blocks raise alerts through rules. Edit its name, description, tags and program, turn its rules off and on, and chart the signals it publishes.

fields.label: Tags
fields.description: Comma-separated.

fields.label: SignalFlow Program

resourceTypes.description: An active alert (incident) raised by a detector rule. Clear it once it is handled.
Silences alert notifications that match a set of dimension filters for a period, optionally recurring. Create one, edit its description, end it early, or delete it.
A group of dashboards. Create, rename and delete groups.
A dashboard of charts inside a dashboard group. Rename it, change its description, or delete it.
A chart on a dashboard: a SignalFlow program and how to draw it. Edit its name, description and program, chart it here, or delete it.
A team of users that owns detectors and dashboards and has its own alert notification policy. Create, rename and delete teams.
A user in the organization. Invite users, grant or revoke admin, or remove them.
A notification, cloud or SSO integration (Slack, PagerDuty, webhook, AWS, GCP, Azure, …). Turn it off and on, validate it, or delete it.
An organization access token for ingest, API or RUM. Edit its description, turn it off and on, rotate its secret (shown once), or delete it.

resourceTypes.description: A service-level objective with its target and compliance window. Delete it here; define it in Splunk.

manifest.description: CI/CD on your own or Buildkite hosted agents. Manage pipelines and their YAML steps, start, cancel and rebuild builds, read job logs, stop and pause agents, and manage clusters, queues, agent tokens, secrets, schedules, pipeline templates and Test Engine flaky tests.

credentialFields.description: Create one under Personal Settings, API Access Tokens, New API Access Token, and give it access to the organization you are connecting. Read scopes: read_organizations, read_pipelines, read_builds, read_build_logs, read_artifacts, read_agents, read_clusters, read_secrets_details, read_pipeline_templates, read_suites, read_teams. To manage things too, add write_pipelines, write_builds, write_agents, write_clusters, write_secrets, write_pipeline_templates and write_suites. The link opens the form with all of them ticked.

resourceTypes.description: The Buildkite organization this connection manages: monthly active users, pipelines, connected agents, running and waiting work, and the API rate limit. Charts builds, failures, build duration and the time jobs wait for an agent across every pipeline.

A pipeline: its repository, cluster, branch rules and YAML steps (edit them in the Steps tab), what is running or waiting right now, its recent builds, and its schedules. Create, edit, archive, unarchive or delete a pipeline, start a build, or move it to another cluster. Charts builds, failures, duration and agent wait time.

resourceTypes.description: A build of a pipeline: state, branch, commit, who started it, how long it ran and waited, its jobs (with Retry, Unblock and logs), annotations and artifacts. Cancel, rebuild or retry failed jobs. The 50 most recent builds in the organization are listed; create one to start a build.
A job in a build: its command, state, exit status, agent and how long it waited for one. The Logs tab tails its output. Retry a failed job, unblock a block step, or change a waiting job's priority.
A connected Buildkite agent: host, version, platform, queue and tags, and the job it is running. Stop it (after its current job, or at once), pause it so it takes no new jobs, or resume it.

A cluster: an isolated group of queues, agents, agent tokens and secrets. Create, edit (name, description, emoji, color, hosted-agent caches) or delete it, choose its default queue, and mint an agent token with Get credentials.

fields.label: Emoji

A private worker pool and its workers. Edit its name, description and labels, cycle its workers, drain or undrain a worker, or delete it.

manifest.description: Self-hosted RabbitMQ through the management API: virtual hosts, exchanges, queues with purge and message peek, bindings, editable policies, users and permissions, connections and channels, shovels and federation, node metrics, and publishing test messages.
manifest.author: Infrawrench

credentialFields.label: Management API URL
credentialFields.description: Where the management plugin listens, including the port: http://mq.example.com:15672 or https://mq.example.com:15671 (rabbitmq-plugins enable rabbitmq_management). For a broker on a private network, add an SSH tunnel or a bastion to this account.

credentialFields.label: Username
credentialFields.description: A user with the administrator tag manages everything; monitoring or policymaker users see less (Check credentials shows what). Create one with rabbitmqctl add_user infrawrench <password> && rabbitmqctl set_user_tags infrawrench administrator && rabbitmqctl set_permissions -p / infrawrench '.*' '.*' '.*'. The guest user only signs in from localhost.

credentialFields.label: OAuth 2 Access Token
credentialFields.description: Only when the broker uses rabbitmq_auth_backend_oauth2 instead of internal users: a JWT from your identity provider, sent as a bearer token. Leave empty to use the username and password.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

capabilities.label: Management API
capabilities.description: Read the overview, virtual hosts, exchanges, queues and bindings.

capabilities.label: Nodes and all connections
capabilities.description: See cluster nodes, their metrics, and every user's connections and channels.

capabilities.label: Policies and parameters
capabilities.description: Manage policies, operator policies, shovels and federation upstreams.

capabilities.label: Users, permissions and definitions
capabilities.description: Manage users, permissions, virtual hosts and limits, and export or import definitions.

resourceTypes.description: The RabbitMQ cluster behind this management endpoint: versions, object totals, queued messages, message rates and alarms. Rename it, export or import definitions, and rebalance queue leaders. The Metrics tab charts message rates and queue depth.

fields.label: Cluster Name
fields.description: Shown in the management UI and reported to clients in server properties.

resourceTypes.description: A cluster node: memory and disk against their alarm thresholds, file descriptors, sockets, Erlang processes, uptime and network partitions. The Metrics tab charts the node's resource use.

postureChecks.title: Node sees a network partition
postureChecks.reason: The node reports partitions with other cluster members; queues may have diverged until the partition is healed.

resourceTypes.description: A virtual host: its own exchanges, queues, bindings, policies and permissions. Create one, edit its description, tags, default queue type, limits and deletion protection, or delete it with everything in it.

fields.label: Tags
fields.description: Comma-separated.

fields.label: Default Queue Type
fields.description: Type given to queues declared without x-queue-type.

fields.label: Max Connections
fields.description: Empty or -1 removes the limit; 0 refuses all client connections.

fields.label: Max Queues
fields.description: Empty or -1 removes the limit.

resourceTypes.description: An exchange and its message rates. Declare one, delete it, see the bindings it routes through, and publish test messages from the Publish tab.

A classic or quorum queue, or a stream: depth, consumers, memory, effective policy and message rates. Declare, purge or delete it, peek at messages in the Describe tab (they are requeued), and publish to it through the default exchange.

orphanRule.reason: The queue has no consumers and no messages.

resourceTypes.description: A binding from an exchange to a queue or another exchange, with its routing key and arguments. Bindings cannot change in place: create a new one and delete the old.

A user policy: queue and exchange settings (TTLs, length limits, dead lettering, federation, quorum group size) applied by name pattern. Create, edit the pattern, priority and JSON definition, or delete it.

fields.label: Pattern
fields.description: Regular expression matched against queue or exchange names.

fields.label: Priority
fields.description: The matching policy with the highest priority wins.

resourceTypes.description: An operator policy: guardrails (max length, TTLs, delivery limits) that cap what user policies can set on queues. Create, edit or delete it.

fields.label: Pattern
fields.description: Regular expression matched against queue or exchange names.

fields.label: Priority
fields.description: The matching policy with the highest priority wins.

resourceTypes.description: A user in RabbitMQ's internal user store (LDAP and OAuth users do not appear). Create one, change its tags, password and connection or channel limits, or delete it.

postureChecks.title: Default guest user exists
postureChecks.reason: The guest user has a well-known password. It is limited to localhost by default, but should be deleted on any shared cluster.

fields.label: Tags
fields.description: Comma-separated: administrator, monitoring, policymaker, management, impersonator.

fields.label: Max Connections
fields.description: Empty or -1 removes the limit.

fields.label: Max Channels
fields.description: Empty or -1 removes the limit.

resourceTypes.description: What a user may configure, write and read in a virtual host, as regular expressions over resource names. Grant, edit or revoke it.
Routing-key restrictions for a user on one topic exchange: which keys it may publish (write) and bind (read) with. Grant, edit or revoke it.
An open client connection (AMQP 0-9-1, AMQP 1.0, MQTT, STOMP): who opened it, from where, with which client, its channels and traffic. Close it from its page.
A channel on a connection: prefetch, unacknowledged messages, consumers and confirm or transaction mode. Read only; close the connection to close its channels.

A dynamic shovel moving messages from a source queue or exchange to a destination, possibly on another broker: state, URIs and counters. Create, restart or delete it. Needs the rabbitmq_shovel_management plugin.

A federation upstream: a remote broker this cluster federates exchanges or queues from, with prefetch, reconnect delay and ack mode, plus the status of its links. Create, edit or delete it; a policy with federation-upstream or federation-upstream-set turns it on.

fields.label: URI
fields.description: amqp:// or amqps:// URI of the upstream.

variables.name: rabbitmq_username
variables.description: Management user with the administrator tag

credentialFields.label: Username
credentialFields.description: Only if the server or the proxy in front of it uses basic auth (web.config.yml basic_auth_users, an nginx or Grafana Cloud style gateway).

credentialFields.description: Instead of basic auth: a bearer token, sent as Authorization: Bearer.

credentialFields.label: Alertmanager URL
credentialFields.description: Optional. Adds silences, notified alerts and receivers: http://alertmanager.internal:9093, or Mimir's /alertmanager. Uses the same credentials.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

capabilities.label: PromQL queries
capabilities.description: Run instant and range queries for the Query and Metrics tabs.

capabilities.label: Targets
capabilities.description: Scrape pools and target health. Thanos, Mimir and VictoriaMetrics may not offer this.

capabilities.label: Rules and alerts
capabilities.description: Recording and alerting rules and active alerts.

capabilities.label: Server status
capabilities.description: Build and runtime information, TSDB statistics and the loaded configuration.

capabilities.label: Alertmanager
capabilities.description: Silences, notified alerts and receivers. Needs an Alertmanager URL on the account.

businessMetricSource.label: Prometheus metric
businessMetricSource.description: Read a Prometheus series, such as requests served or orders placed, and store one value per day.

fields.label: Metric
fields.description: Every metric name the server knows. Counters usually end in _total.

fields.label: Label filter
fields.description: Optional PromQL label matchers, without the braces.

fields.label: Break down by
fields.description: Optional label. Each value becomes its own label on the metric.

options.label: The last value of the day

resourceTypes.description: The Prometheus-compatible server this connection queries (Prometheus, Thanos Query, Mimir, Cortex or VictoriaMetrics): version, retention, head series, target health, rules and firing alerts. Run PromQL in the Query tab, read the loaded configuration, reload it, and use the TSDB admin tools. The Metrics tab charts ingestion, series and target health.

postureChecks.title: Last configuration reload failed
postureChecks.reason: Prometheus is still running the previous configuration; the file on disk has an error.

resourceTypes.description: A scrape job and the targets it discovered, with how many are up. Read its effective configuration with secrets redacted.
A scrape target: its labels, scrape URL, health, last error and scrape duration. The Metrics tab charts up, scrape duration and samples scraped.
A group of recording and alerting rules from a rule file: interval, evaluation time and the health of its rules. Rules are defined in files on the server, so they are read only here.
A recording or alerting rule: its expression, for duration, labels and annotations, health and last error, and for alerting rules its state and active alerts. The Metrics tab charts the expression.
An active alert in Prometheus (pending or firing), with its labels, annotations, value and since when. Silence it when an Alertmanager is connected.
The Alertmanager connected to this account: version, cluster state and peers, uptime and its configuration (read only). Silences, alerts and receivers live under it.
An Alertmanager silence: the label matchers it mutes, when it starts and ends, who created it and why. Create one, extend it or change its comment, or expire it.

fields.label: Matchers
fields.description: Comma-separated, e.g. alertname="DiskFull", instance=~"db-.*".

fields.label: Ends
fields.description: An ISO time, or a duration from now such as 2h or 3d.

resourceTypes.description: An alert as Alertmanager sees it: which receivers it routes to and whether a silence or an inhibition mutes it. Silence it from its page.
A notification receiver defined in the Alertmanager configuration.

resourceTypes.description: A service, batch, system or sysbatch job, periodic or parameterized: status, type, priority, version and task group counts. Run one from HCL, edit and resubmit its specification, stop, start, scale a group, dispatch, force a periodic run, revert to an earlier version, or stop and purge it.

An ACL policy. Read and edit its HCL rules, create policies, or delete them.

A CSI storage plugin and the health of its controller and node instances.
A service registered in Nomad's native service discovery, with its tags and every registered instance (address, port, allocation and node).

capabilities.label: Catalog and health

capabilities.label: Key/value store

capabilities.label: Intentions and config entries
capabilities.description: Read and write intentions and configuration entries.

capabilities.label: ACL policies, roles and tokens

fields.label: Action
fields.description: L4 intentions only; L7 intentions use permissions.

resourceTypes.description: A centralised configuration entry: service defaults, proxy defaults, routers, splitters, resolvers, intentions, gateways and routes, mesh, exported services and more. Edit it as JSON, create one from a starter document, or delete it.
An ACL policy: HCL rules, description and the datacenters it applies in. Create, edit its rules and description, or delete it.

fields.label: Datacenters
fields.description: Comma-separated; empty means all.

resourceTypes.description: An ACL role: a named set of policies and service or node identities that tokens can carry. Create, edit or delete it.

fields.label: Policies
fields.description: Comma-separated policy names.

fields.label: Service Identities
fields.description: Comma-separated service names.

resourceTypes.description: An ACL token by accessor: description, policies, roles, service and node identities, whether it is local, and when it expires. Create, edit or delete it.

postureChecks.title: Token carries global-management
postureChecks.reason: global-management bypasses every ACL rule. Keep such tokens few, and prefer scoped policies.

fields.label: Policies
fields.description: Comma-separated policy names.

fields.label: Roles
fields.description: Comma-separated role names.

fields.label: Service Identities
fields.description: Comma-separated service names.

resourceTypes.description: A session: the node and checks it is tied to, its TTL and behaviour, and the locks it holds. Renew or destroy it.

A cluster peering connection: state, the peer's server name and addresses, and how many services are imported and exported. Generate a peering token for another cluster, establish a peering from one, or delete it.
A Consul Enterprise namespace. Create, edit its description and metadata, or delete it.

fields.label: Metadata
fields.description: Comma-separated key=value pairs.

resourceTypes.description: A Consul Enterprise admin partition. Create, edit its description, or delete it.

manifest.description: Self-hosted NATS through a server's monitoring endpoint: server health and limits, routes, gateways and leaf nodes, accounts, connections, and JetStream streams, key-value buckets and consumers with their progress. Read only.
manifest.author: Infrawrench

credentialFields.label: Monitoring URL
credentialFields.description: The server's HTTP monitoring endpoint, not the client port: http://nats.internal:8222 (enable it with http_port: 8222 in the server config, or -m 8222). Include the http_base_path if one is set. For a server on a private network, add an SSH tunnel to this account.

credentialFields.label: Username
credentialFields.description: Only if a reverse proxy in front of the monitoring port asks for basic auth; nats-server itself has none there.

credentialFields.label: Bearer Token
credentialFields.description: Only if a reverse proxy in front of the monitoring port expects a bearer token.

credentialFields.label: CA Certificate (optional)
credentialFields.description: PEM-encoded trust anchor for verifying the API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted vendor instances or corporate TLS-intercepting proxies. Leave blank to use the operating system's default trust store.

capabilities.label: Server information
capabilities.description: Read /varz: version, connections, traffic and limits.

capabilities.label: JetStream
capabilities.description: Read /jsz: accounts, streams and consumers.

capabilities.label: Accounts
capabilities.description: Read /accountz and /accstatz.

resourceTypes.description: The nats-server behind this monitoring endpoint: version, cluster, connections and subscriptions, traffic, slow consumers, routes, gateways and leaf nodes, JetStream usage against its limits, and health. The Metrics tab records connections, memory, CPU and JetStream storage.
A route to another server in the cluster, a gateway to another cluster, or a leaf node connection: remote name, address, round trip time, traffic and subscriptions.
A NATS account: connections, leaf nodes, subscriptions, messages sent and received, slow consumers, and its JetStream storage, memory, streams and consumers.
A JetStream stream (or a key-value bucket or object store, which are streams underneath): subjects, retention, storage, replicas and limits, messages, bytes, sequence range, and its cluster leader.

postureChecks.title: Stream has a single replica
postureChecks.reason: A stream with one replica loses its messages if that server's storage is lost.

resourceTypes.description: A JetStream consumer: push or pull, deliver and ack policies, filter subjects, and its progress (pending, waiting for ack, redelivered, delivered and acknowledged sequences).
An open client connection: name, address, account and user, client library and version, uptime, idle time, round trip, subscriptions, traffic and bytes pending.

variables.name: nats_credentials
variables.description: Contents of a NATS .creds file for an account allowed to manage JetStream
